name: The Field household at 1919 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_field_marshall_jr

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1919 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1919 Mr. & Mrs. Marshall Field jr..

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1919, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. A house of this kind kept live-in staff, and the 1900 and 1910 censuses name them; neither was read for this card, so no staff are listed. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Albertine Huck Field
persons.note: The Blue Book prints her as Mrs. Marshall Field jr.; her own name is from Wikipedia's article on her son, which calls her the daughter of Louis Carl Huck.

persons.name: Marshall Field III
persons.note: Ten years old on the scene date. Wikipedia names his parents and says he was 'raised primarily in England' (after his father's death in 1905) without giving a Chicago address; his place in his parents' house in 1904 is inferred.

persons.name: Henry Field

born.note: Born 1895, died 1917 (the lifespan Wikipedia's article on his brother gives him).

persons.note: About nine on the scene date; his place in his parents' house is inferred as his brother's is. A sister, Gwendolyn, is not on this card because the source read for it does not name her.
